issue.body:
Found by the #386 evaluation (`docs/evaluation/editorial-386/`), row `case-study-sv`, Redline half. Both blind judges fail `G2` and `R1` on it, for one root cause.

**What happened.** The draft arrived with a conforming headline, *Elm Quay testade gemensam logg i två hus*. The review found it said nothing of the angle; the one correction round replaced it with *Gemensam logg hjälpte Elm Quay men kostade förberedelsetid*. The re-review then found — correctly, and reported it in exemplary detail — that the new headline claims in the publication's voice an effect the body explicitly withholds (the text attributes "hjälper oss" to Maya Lind alone, and says the note does not attribute the shorter time to the software). The loop stopped on "a finding an earlier round's own repair created", the budget being spent as well, and the text was **delivered with the worse headline in place**, as an unresolved finding. The source, which Redline never sees, forbids exactly that claim.

**Why it is a defect and not a budget question.** Step 7 of `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` rejects a returned correction and keeps the pre-round Text Artifact in one case only: a claim that sat beside the defect was lost. A repair that *adds* an unsupported claim, or otherwise leaves a passage worse than it arrived, stops the loop but stays in the delivered text. Undoing it needed nothing the run lacked: it held the pre-round text.

**Seen elsewhere the same day**, in staged runs of `main` that are not protocol records: `column-flawed` — the round's new headline repeated the standfirst the same round had written; `opinion-flawed` — the new headline's "ett halvår till" presupposes an earlier half-year the text never states; `article-flawed` (#386) — a subheading the round added repeats the sentence under it. In each case the re-review caught it and the delivery carried it. The new headline, standfirst and subheadings a correction round writes are where it happens.

**Evidence.** `docs/evaluation/editorial-386/runs/case-study-sv/redline/` — `work/input.md`, `response.md`, `delivered.md`, `judgement-a.md`, `judgement-b.md`.

Open for triage: whether a repair-created finding that names an unsupported or strengthened claim should reject that repair the way a lost claim does (restoring the pre-round passage and carrying the original finding forward), and whether that reaches every repair-created finding or only those that move a claim.

Related: #383 (changes outside any finding, and accounts that omit them) — a different hole; this one is a reported change that should not have been kept.

> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

Thomas approved this scope on 2026-09-21. This comment settles the body's open question: rejection covers every verified repair-created defect, not only changes to claims. Where this comment is silent, the body and earlier requirements stand. Read the whole thread before building.

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** Reject an entire correction round when independent re-review establishes that it introduced a defect, restore its pre-round Text Artifact, and stop.

### What triage established

The saved #386 case-study-sv response delivers the strengthened headline and explicitly identifies it as unsupported by its own body. The column and article evidence also shows repair-created echoes. The current Redline contract rejects certain claim losses and weakened limits, but otherwise stops on a repair-created finding while allowing the defective correction to remain. This was verified against the saved artifacts and shipped contract, not by a fresh native run during triage. No prior rejection record was found.

### What to build

Treat a correction as a candidate until the independent review of that candidate has established whether it introduced a defect. If re-review verifies a defect absent before the responsible correction, reject that entire correction, restore its complete pre-round Text Artifact verbatim, and stop the substantive correction loop. This applies to unsupported or strengthened claims, lost qualifications, echoes and any other defect under the loaded contract. A preference or an old defect first noticed later is not automatically a repair-created defect: establish the change and the violated requirement against the retained states.

If a defect is discovered only after a later round, restore the state immediately before the round that introduced it and discard the later dependent states too. Findings accompanying the restored text must describe that text: carry forward its unresolved findings, and report the rejected attempt separately rather than describing its discarded defect as still present.

The attempted correction still spends its budget. Restoration spends no additional budget, refunds none, and authorizes no new wording or compensating correction. Retain earlier accepted work only insofar as it is present in the restored state. Run the existing closing installed Proofread pass exactly once after the substantive loop stops, and make no substantive edit after it.

Preserve the existing claim-loss and limiting-sentence protections. Preserve #383's separate rule for differences that trace to no commissioning finding: those passages are restored before the candidate is reviewed. A candidate that survives that check can still introduce a defect, which is what this ticket rejects. Keep the delivery's itemized claim account and closing summary truthful about what was attempted, rejected and ultimately retained.

Sweep Redline's shipped instructions, correction brief and help, and any shared prose that states the changed duty.

### Key interfaces

- The retained Text Artifact states, correction candidate and independent re-review findings.
- Correction Budget accounting and the repair-created-finding stop condition.
- #383's change-to-finding check and the final delivery account.
- The closing installed Proofread invocation.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A verified newly introduced defect rejects the whole responsible correction and restores the pre-round artifact verbatim before the closing mechanical pass.
- [ ] A newly introduced unsupported headline and a newly introduced heading echo both exercise rejection in focused native regressions.
- [ ] A mixed round containing a valid repair and a new defect is rejected as a whole; a defect discovered one round later restores the state before the introducing round.
- [ ] Existing findings that merely persist or are newly noticed do not cause false attribution to a repair; a clean, justified correction can still be accepted.
- [ ] Rejection stops the loop, spends the attempted budget without refund, carries the restored text's unresolved findings, and truthfully distinguishes discarded defects from defects left in delivery.
- [ ] #383's restoration of untraced differences, existing claim/limit protections, and exactly one closing installed Proofread pass remain intact.
- [ ] Preserve native regression evidence under the focused-regression conventions, including exact invocation, pre-round/candidate/restored text and observed sequence. If controlled correction returns are needed to exercise the boundary, disclose that setup rather than calling it an unprompted reproduction. No source material is supplied to Redline.
- [ ] The four checks in CONTRIBUTING.md pass and the Catalog is regenerated.

### Out of scope

Increasing the Correction Budget; partial acceptance of a defective round; another repair attempt after rejection; Source Fidelity checks or access to external source material; changing Unslop; #383's independent diagnostic/accounting work.

### Blocked by

#383. It changes the same candidate-acceptance boundary and delivery account. Build on its completed result, retaining its change-to-finding check before applying this rejection rule. The native blocked-by relation carries this dependency.

## The later-discovery clause is carried by the contract, not by a run

Settled by Thomas on 2026-09-23, in answer to a question the Orchestrate run working this ticket put to him. This comment is written by that run to record his answer where the work can read it.

**The question.** The second clause of the third acceptance criterion — *a defect discovered one round later restores the state before the introducing round* — was not established by any preserved native run, and two independent verifications established that it cannot be staged. The clause needs a re-review to **miss** a defect that a later re-review then catches. The re-review is the Redline run's own parent agent rather than a delegated subagent, so criterion 7's sanctioned controlled correction return cannot reach it: there is no party to intercept. Thirty-one native runs across seven frozen waves, eight of them reaching a second round, produced five rejections and every one of them at round 1, which is where the rule is meant to fire.

**The answer.** The clause is met by the contract prose in `skills/editorial/redline/SKILL.md` and the test that holds that prose in place. It is not required to be demonstrated by a native run, because no run can be made to demonstrate it. Nothing else in the criterion is relaxed: the mixed-round half stands as an observed result, and every other criterion stands exactly as written and as already measured.

**What this does not license.** The rule itself is unchanged — a defect established after a later round still restores the state immediately before the round that introduced it and discards every state built on it. What changes is only what counts as evidence for that one clause. No criterion is softened for want of a result elsewhere, no frozen plan or artefact is edited to fit this, and the packet says plainly which clause is carried by prose rather than by a run.

**Still owed on this ticket.** The evidence packet records the clause as unmet by any run; it should now record that it is settled as carried by the contract, naming this comment, so a later reader does not find an open gap with no resolution beside it. The behaviour that no run reached is worth its own `needs-triage` issue naming this ticket, so that a future evaluation with a way to observe it can pick it up.
